knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Polynomial Raised to a Power Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=g^{2},\,g=x^{4} - 4 x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=2g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=4 x^{3} - 4.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=2g\cdot (4 x^{3} - 4) \\  &=2(x^{4} - 4 x)(4 x^{3} - 4).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x)=(2 x^{2} - 5)^{4},$ find the slope at the point $(2,81)$
question.:question/worked-solution:

We use the chain rule to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}.$

$$

$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=4g^{3},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=4 x.
$$

Multiplying the two together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=4g^{3}\cdot (4 x) \\  &=16 x(2 x^{2} - 5)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|_{x=2} &=[16 x(2 x^{2} - 5)^{3}]|_{x=2} \\  &=16 (2)(2 (2)^{2} - 5)^{3} \\  &=864.\end{aligned}

To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}.$

First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=g^{4},\,g=3-2x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=4g^{3},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-2.
$$

Multiplying the two together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=4g^{3}\cdot (-2) \\  &=-8(3-2x)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line at the point where $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|_{x=1} &=-8(3-2(1))^{3} \\  &=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(1,1)$ is $m=-8.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(1) &=-8(x-(1)) \\ y-(1) &=8 - 8 x \\ y &=9 - 8 x\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x)=(-1+2x)^{4},$ find the equation of the tangent at point $(1,1)$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}.$

First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=g^{4},\,g=-1+2x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=4g^{3},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

Multiplying the two together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=4g^{3}\cdot (2) \\  &=8(-1+2x)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line at the point where $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|_{x=1} &=8(-1+2(1))^{3} \\  &=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(1,1)$ is $m=8.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(1) &=8(x-(1)) \\ y-(1) &=8 x - 8 \\ y &=8 x - 7\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x)=(5+3x)^{3},$ find the equation of the tangent at point $(-1,8)$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}.$

First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=g^{3},\,g=5+3x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=3g^{2},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

Multiplying the two together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=3g^{2}\cdot (3) \\  &=9(5+3x)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line at the point where $x=-1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|_{x=-1} &=9(5+3(-1))^{2} \\  &=36.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(-1,8)$ is $m=36.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(8) &=36(x-(-1)) \\ y-(8) &=36 x + 36 \\ y &=36 x + 44\end{aligned}
$$
